_verify: VERIFIED 2026-10-11 (Wikipedia): 1656, Prado; Infanta Margaret Theresa, age five; maid María Agustina Sarmiento kneels offering a drink in a red cup; dwarfs Mari Bárbola and Nicolás Pertusato, who prods a sleepy mastiff with his foot; José Nieto Velázquez, the queen's chamberlain, in the doorway; mirror shows King Philip IV and Queen Mariana (debate: the couple standing where the viewer is, or the canvas Velázquez paints); Velázquez knighted in Order of Santiago 1659, died 1660; Palomino: Philip ordered the cross added after his death.

slides.headline: Who is really being painted here?
Madrid, 1656
slides.text: A room in the royal palace. A little princess, her maids, two dwarfs, a dog. And several of them are looking at you.

slides.headline: At the center, the princess
slides.text: Margaret Theresa, five years old. A maid kneels and offers her a drink in a red cup.

slides.headline: But the painter is here too
slides.text: Velázquez stands at a huge canvas, brush in hand, looking straight out. At whom?

slides.headline: The answer is in the mirror
slides.text: At the back: King Philip IV and Queen Mariana. So they stand exactly where you are standing.

slides.headline: Meanwhile, at the door
slides.text: The queen's chamberlain stops on the stairs and looks back. Coming in, or leaving?

slides.headline: Not everyone is posing
slides.text: Down in front, a boy puts his foot on the sleepy mastiff. The dog doesn't even move.

slides.headline: And one detail came later
slides.text: The red cross on the painter's chest. He was knighted in 1659, three years after finishing this.

slides.headline: So who added it?
slides.text: Velázquez died in 1660. The story goes that the king had the cross added. And the canvas? We still can't see it.
